headline: HOUSEHOLD 💰 ENERGY 📈 BILLS 🧾 Set For BIGGEST 🏔️ RISE 📈 In FOUR 🕒 YEARS 🗓️
text: Typical 🏠 households 🏡 are staring 😶 down the barrel 🔫 of an annual 💸 gas 🔥 and electricity ⚡ bill 🧾 hitting £1,999 💷 from January ❄️ according to the latest forecast 🔮 from Cornwall 🌽 Insight 🧠. Energy 🛢️ prices 📈 are about to SOAR 🦅 with a predicted £276 💷 jump that slams 🚪 millions of homes 🏘️ right when it's the COLDEST 🥶 time of year and marks the biggest rise 📈 in four whole years 🗓️. This forecast 📊 dropped just before Ofgem's October price cap 🧢 hikes kick in putting massive pressure 🗜️ on the government 🏛️ to step up and support those who will struggle 💸 to pay their dues. Meanwhile the boss 🕴️ of supplier EDF Simone Rossi has warned we're "walking 🚶‍♂️ into a second energy crisis" and is begging 🙏 for an extension on that VAT cut ✂️ which starts Thursday. About 20 million 🧮 households across England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 and Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿 sit on variable tariffs set by Ofgem's price cap 🧢 which limits the max price per unit of gas 🔥 and electricity ⚡ so those homes will see a 4% increase on Thursday equaling roughly £60 💷 a year or £5 monthly taking the typical bill to £1,723 if it held steady all year long. That rise would have been even steeper without the government's VAT cut ✂️ which shaves off about £45 yearly from a standard bill but forecasts now scream a far bigger 16% spike is coming in January pushing the typical annual bill straight to £1,999 according to Cornwall 🌽 Insight. The predicted rise hits households hard 🥊 in January already a brutal month with freezing ❄️ weather and bank accounts still bruised from Christmas 🎄 spending Craig Lowrey principal consultant at Cornwall Insight explained. These prices are going to hit households hard he said and the surge comes from disrupted gas supplies due to the conflict in the Middle East plus super low storage levels across Europe meaning rebuilding those stocks could keep bills sky high well beyond winter according to the respected forecaster. Cornwall Insight has a rock solid track record on these predictions and similar warnings have come from energy suppliers too so this remains a forecast for now with Ofgem set to announce the real January price change late in November. While easing tensions in the Middle East might soften the blow the price setting window for January is already halfway done and with no clear truce or dropping international costs a massive increase for anyone not locked into a fixed tariff looks all but certain Lowrey confirmed. That will hammer people like Aaron Richards from Maidenhead who says it feels like all his costs are climbing he tries to eat fewer takeaways works extra overtime and budgets tighter but insists we shouldn't have to. Aaron drives a diesel car paying record prices at the pump to get to and from work and just feels like everything's going up how far will it go someone's got to step in. He knows folks who can't even afford to heat their house and are struggling right now saying housing and eating are life's essentials that everyone should have without it being a constant battle. Years of high domestic energy bills have left some drowning in debt with recent Ofgem data showing customers collectively owe more than £5 billion in unpaid bills and charges to suppliers. The regulator has a proposed debt relief scheme ready on the table and campaigners are yelling at them to implement it fast while urging the government to fund it properly. This is unsustainable not just for households but for the whole market Adam Scorer chief executive of fuel poverty charity National Energy Action stated. The Budget must deliver targeted support for the most at risk this winter plus real action on energy debt and upgrading the least efficient homes he demanded. Among those calling for urgent government help is Simone Rossi chief executive of EDF Energy who told the BBC we're actually walking into a second significant energy crisis after the one from four years ago. He pushed for extending the VAT cut on electricity bills from 5% to 0% past April when it expires and also urged ministers to approve the new Jackdaw gas field off Aberdeen and the Rosebank oil field off Shetland. The government keeps saying it will look at ways to give billpayers some breathing room on the cost of living crisis.
